title: Ops Sidecar: Pilot QuickPlays (notes, draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, action-first note set for SEs + Ops to run a pilot with an ‘ops sidecar’ mindset: seller stays customer-facing; ops runs the safe-guard, rollbacks, and fast experiments in the background. NOT a full PRD — quick plays, scripts, and canary checks to keep pilots alive and measurable.

Audience
- Sales Engineers (primary)
- Platform/Ops on-call (secondary)
- Solutions Engineers / Customer Success (supporting)

High-level goals
- Make pilots resiliant: reduce time-to-recover for customer-facing failures to <15m
- Capture metrics early: latency, error-rate, token-USD cost, quota headroom
- Rapidly validate integration and rollback safely without interrupting customer demos

Three QuickPlays (ops-sidecar patterns)
1) Canary Mirroring (safe smoke)
  - What: Mirror 5–10% of production pilot calls to a parallel route (read-only). Don't return mirrored output to user; log diff and quality metrics.
  - Why: Catch quality regressions from model/quantization changes without impacting the UX.
  - Runbook (ops):
    * Deploy mirror route using routing policy: traffic_split=95/5 to primary/mirror.
    * Confirm mirror flags: anonymize user id, mask PII, enable verbose logging for first 1k tokens.
    * Monitor: drift-alert if top-1 token disagreement > 8% across 100 examples.
  - Seller script:
    * "We're running a brief safety mirror on a small portion of requests to ensure performance — nothing changes for your users."

2) Fast Fallback (cost & latency guard)
  - What: On sustained latency or OOMs, automatically route to a cheaper / smaller model variant and return a short contextual note.
  - Why: Maintain availability and predictable latency during spikes.
  - Runbook (ops):
    * Policy: if p95 latency > 700ms for >2 minutes OR GPU errors >= 3/min, switch to fallback model variant for 10m, then evaluate.
    * Telemetry: tag fallback events with customer_id and rollback_reason.
    * Postmortem trigger: any fallback > 15m -> create incident and SE handoff.
  - Seller script:
    * "You might see a brief change in response style while we balance capacity — we’ll revert within minutes and share a note if you want to review outputs."

3) Prefix Caching Warmup (reduce cold start tail)
  - What: For pilot flows with repeated system prompts, pre-warm KV cache using synthetic warmup calls during ramp windows.
  - Why: Avoid token tax from cold KV loads and stabilize p99 latency for interactive demos.
  - Runbook (ops):
    * Schedule warmup job 5 minutes before demo start. Job sends 50 warmup requests with masked customer ids.
    * Observe cache-hit rate target >= 85% after warmup.
  - Seller script:
    * "We run a short warmup before demos so the first live interactions feel snappy — nothing you do is stored in your account."

Canary checklist (pre-pilot)
- Confirm model pin/version for pilot (exact tag)
- Make a clear fallback mapping table (model->fallback) and pre-configure routing policy
- Agree on SLIs and dashboard links with customer: latency, errors, cost burn rate
- Set alert thresholds and a single on-call alias for pilot window
- Run quick privacy check: no raw PII to external logs, KMS keys validated

Emergency triage flow (concise)
1) SE notices anomaly -> ping #pilot-ops Slack with customer_id + concise symptoms (latency, mismatch, cost spike)
2) Ops sidecar takes control: flip to fallback, or scale capacity, or toggle mirror off
3) Ops documents action in ticket (Jira) and posts rollback note in Slack
4) SE resumes customer-facing narrative after one-line confirmation: "Ops applied a temporary route; demo continues."

Escalation matrix (if sidecar can't fix)
- Level 1 (on-call ops): aim 0–15m recovery, use fallback routing.
- Level 2 (platform eng): if recovery > 30m or repeated OOMs, engage platform-engineering@redwood.
- Level 3 (product/exec): if pilot outage threatens deal close within 72h, notify product and your AE.

Metrics to capture (minimum)
- Request-level: customer_id, route, model_version, latency_ms, verdict (success/error), token_count, cost_est_usd
- Aggregates: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, fallback rate, diff-rate (mirror disagreement)
- Business: average cost per happy session, conversions per 1k calls

Slide deck mapping (what to include in a 6-slide sales enablement mini-deck)
1) One-liner + problem we solve (pilot instability, unpredictable cost)
2) Ops Sidecar concept visual (traffic split, mirror, fallback)
3) QuickPlay examples (three plays, one-liners)
4) Seller scripts + FAQ (what to tell customer)
5) Dashboards & telemetry snapshot (mock charts)
6) Runbook anchor + next steps (who to ping, ticket templates)

Seller FAQs (short answers sellers can paste)
Q: Will this change my demo output?
A: No — mirrored traffic is invisible and fallbacks are temporary with a contextual note.
Q: What about data retention?
A: Pilot sidecar logs are scrubbed and expire per our pilot policy (14 days) unless customer requests longer.
Q: Can we disable the sidecar?
A: Yes — but we strongly recommend it for the first 24–72h of the pilot to avoid surprises.

Notes to self (TODOs)
- Build a lightweight dashboard template for mirror-diff metrics (Ravi)
- Add canned Jira templates and Slack snippet (Sofia)
- Draft one-pager for legal on pilot log retention (Marco)
- Run a dry-run with internal sales team next week (schedule)

Rough templates (copy-paste snippets)
Slack alert snippet:
  "PILOT-ALERT: customer=AcmeCo, symptom=high-p95-latency, route=prod, time=14:12PT -- ops oncall please. Link: <JIRA-XXXX>"
Jira incident summary template:
  "Pilot incident - <customer> - <short symptom> - action taken: <fallback|scale|rollback> - duration: <mins>"
SE opening script for pilot kickoff:
  "Hi — for the pilot we'll run a safety sidecar to make sure we can act fast without interrupting your users. We'll share a brief note after the pilot summarizing any changes."

Appendix: useful links / configs
- Pilot routing policy example: // link to internal yaml snippet (see linked_artifacts)
- Sidecar playbook badge: internal doc id PILOT-OP-2025

End of draft — this is intentionally concise and playbook-focused. Looking for feedback on alert thresholds and seller phrasing before converting to a 4-slide enablement pocket deck.
